findings.title: add_members/remove_member routes don't include group id in path
findings.body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are nested under `resources :groups` collection-style without a member block, so they map to `/admin/groups/members` instead of `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`. The controller actions rely on `params.require(:group_id)`, which must then be passed as a query/body param instead of a path segment, inconsistent with the group.js model which calls `/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'`. This mismatch means the JS-generated URLs (e.g. `/admin/groups/5/members.json`) will not match this route definition at all, causing 404s for add/remove member actions from the admin UI.

findings.title: findMembers silently returns undefined for group with no name, breaking promise chains
findings.body: `findMembers` returns `undefined` (via bare `return;`) when name is empty, but callers like `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` call `model.findMembers()` without checking the return value, and other callers (`removeMember`, `addMembers`) chain `.then()` on it. If `findMembers` is ever called in that state (e.g. a group being created, with no name yet) any subsequent chained `.then()` would throw since `undefined.then` is not a function. The previous code safely returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`; this behavior was removed without updating all callers to tolerate it.

findings.title: members action performs an extra count query without an existing index verified
findings.body: The new `members` action calls `group.users.count` for `total` and a separate paginated query, resulting in two queries instead of one previously. For large automatic groups (previously limited to 200), this adds overhead on every page load. Not necessarily wrong, but a potential performance regression worth confirming is acceptable given removal of the previous automatic-group-only limit comment about truncation bugs with >200 groups, which is no longer mentioned or addressed here as a known limitation goes unverified for all group types now (always paginated with limit 50).

findings.title: add_members/remove_member endpoints lack explicit automatic-group checks consistency with destroy/update
findings.body: Both `add_members` and `remove_member` guard against automatic groups via `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`, which is good, but there is no spec covering case where `group_id` doesn't exist (invalid id leads to ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, unhandled -> 500 instead of a clean 404). This isn't newly introduced but the PR adds these actions without addressing error handling for missing groups, which could leak 500 errors instead of friendly 404s in production for malformed requests.
